title: Enforcement that python -O cannot delete
note: D-2026-73. EA1 turns one real enforcement -- I4, the proposer may not verify its own record -- into an assert: the -O probe must see it allowed, and the repository-wide scan must see the assert. EA2 narrows the scan to a list of directories, the scope that once missed a root module. EA3 lets the scan count a file's asserts and pass regardless.

mutations.name: EA1_a_refusal_is_an_assert_again
mutations.find:
if req.actor == req.proposer:
            raise TransitionError(
                f"I4: {req.actor!r} proposed {req.record_id} and may not also "
                f"perform {req.src.value} -> {req.dst.value}")
mutations.replace:
assert req.actor != req.proposer, (
                f"I4: {req.actor!r} proposed {req.record_id} and may not also "
                f"perform {req.src.value} -> {req.dst.value}")
mutations.rationale: I4 holds only while asserts run: under python -O the proposer verifies its own record, and the repository-wide scan must see the assert

mutations.name: EA2_the_scan_is_a_list_of_directories
mutations.replace:
files = [f for f in repository_files("*.py", include_tests=False)
             if f.startswith(("scientific/", "scientific_ai/", "tools/"))]
mutations.rationale: the scope that once missed a root module: the substrate and the root scripts are never scanned

mutations.name: EA3_found_asserts_are_counted_and_ignored
mutations.rationale: the scan finds the asserts and the rule never refuses them
